evidence.title: Automated search found benign-framed training data with misaligned generalization
evidence.observation: Anthropic reports an automated search for fine-tuning data that passed a training-data monitor while inducing misalignment in research models. Agents used a shared experiment log; successful data often framed behavior as fiction or roleplay.
evidence.evidence_standing: Source-reported bounded observation; not independently verified

source_locations.SRC-156: Introduction; Setup; results and example datasets

evidence.limitations: The red team had access to the exact monitor and unrestricted synthetic-data design. Models were deliberately trained for this experiment and never deployed. Results do not establish deployed Claude behavior or failure of every defense; fixed evaluation scoring can reward framing as well as actions.
evidence.open_questions: Do the findings generalize beyond the reported setting? Underlying results and mechanisms are not independently reproduced.

terms.name: Cross-system feedback
terms.definition: A pattern in which an action or output from one technical or organizational process affects activity elsewhere and subsequent responses modify conditions for additional participants. Many response paths may exist; there need not be a single linear loop.

terms.name: Observability boundary
terms.definition: The practical limit of what a given observer or monitoring arrangement can detect, interpret, or causally connect. The limit may be known, partly understood, or itself unrecognized.
